exercise.name: Overhead Sit-up with Legs on Bench

reference.title: Overhead Sit-up with Legs on Bench (male)
reference.listing: GymVisual page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching knowledge

exercise.mechanics: Trunk flexion with the arms as a long lever

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you swing the arms and sit up, inhale as you roll back down.
breathing.cadence: About 1.4 s up, short pause, 2 s down

prescription.tempo: About 1.4 s up, short pause, 2 s down
prescription.progression: Keep the arms beside the ears all the way up (longer lever), then hold a light plate overhead

cues.text: Lie on your back with the calves resting on a flat bench, hips and knees about 90 degrees. Arms straight overhead on the mat.
Breathe out, bring the straight arms up over the face and curl the head and shoulders off the mat.
Keep curling and sit up, reaching the hands past the knees toward the feet.
Brief pause at the top; calves stay on the bench.
Breathe in and roll back down slowly, arms returning overhead as the shoulders reach the mat.
Arms rest overhead; repeat without bouncing.

mistakes.mistake: Throwing the arms to jerk up
mistakes.fix: Bring the arms up with the curl, not ahead of it.
Keep the calves heavy on the bench.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back with the arms overhead
mistakes.fix: Brace so the low back stays on the mat at the start.

kinematics.measure: Trunk (pelvis to C7) from the floor
kinematics.norm: From lying to sitting up near the thighs (clinical opinion)
Starts at about 90 degrees with the calves on the bench and closes as you sit up; hip flexors take over in the second half of a sit-up (Andersson 1997)
Straight overhead on the mat at the start, reaching past the knees at the top (clinical opinion)
The upper back curls first (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1.4 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #17894, Overhead Sit-up with Legs on Bench (male), video (movement reference; page not readable here)
Andersson, Nilsson, Ma and Thorstensson 1997, abdominal and hip flexor muscle activation during various training exercises (Eur J Appl Physiol 75:115-123; PMID 9118976)
Escamilla, Lewis, Pecson, Imamura and Andrews 2016, muscle activation among supine, prone and side position exercises with and without a Swiss ball (Sports Health 8(4):372-379; PMC4922527)
Axler and McGill 1997, low-back loads over a variety of abdominal exercises: searching for the safest abdominal challenge (Med Sci Sports Exerc 29(6):804-811)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Full sit-ups load the low back more than curl-ups (McGill 1998; Axler and McGill 1997).
Low-back pain or flexion intolerance: choose a curl-up, dead bug or plank instead.
Shoulder pain overhead: start with the arms crossed on the chest.
modify: Shoulder or neck discomfort: arms crossed on the chest.
Low back discomfort: stop halfway (curl-up with the legs on the bench).
regressions: Crunch with the legs on a bench.
Sit-up with the arms reaching forward.
progressions: Arms beside the ears all the way up.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis curls the trunk; the straight arms overhead lengthen the lever at the start (clinical opinion). Bent-knee sit-ups gave about 35-40% MVIC in the rectus abdominis (Escamilla 2016).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: With the calves on the bench the hips start at about 90 degrees; iliopsoas still helps sit up once the shoulder blades are off the mat (Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: With the calves on the bench the hips start at about 90 degrees; iliopsoas still helps sit up once the shoulder blades are off the mat (Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Front deltoids bring the straight arms from overhead to forward (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Front deltoids bring the straight arms from overhead to forward (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Arms sweep from overhead to the knees
